---
title: "Install the advanced source workflow"
---

::: {.callout-note}
For ordinary Python use or the installed `uv run metis train` Hydra interface, start
with the [package quickstart](../package/quickstart.qmd). That workflow supports
CPU training and saves portable artifacts in a uv-managed project.

This page covers the historical `train.py` workflow in a source checkout. It
exposes advanced CUDA/DDP and sequence-conditioning settings, requires a
compatible CUDA PyTorch installation and NVIDIA GPU, and uses a different
checkpoint format.
:::

## Set up a source checkout

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Git, then run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git
cd metis
uv sync --locked --all-extras
```

This includes the development tools and all optional dependencies, including
the historical trainer's plotting, terminal and Weights & Biases dependencies.
uv creates `.venv` using the versions in `uv.lock`; you do not need to activate
it. Base-package installation alone does not supply the historical dependencies.

The checkout defaults to CPU PyTorch on Linux and Windows and a PyPI platform
build on Apple Silicon macOS; Intel Macs are unsupported by the current PyTorch
dependency range. **The historical trainer requires an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA
PyTorch.** Before running it, use the
[CUDA named-index setup](../package/quickstart.qmd#optional-cuda-setup) to change
your local torch source and lockfile to suit your driver. Then synchronize the
checkout again with `uv sync --locked --all-extras`. Installing Python
dependencies does not configure GPU drivers or establish GPU compatibility.

Keep all extras explicit when running historical recipes:

```bash
uv run --locked --all-extras python train.py --config-name default
```

The all-extras environment includes the Python dependencies used by historical
notebooks and documentation. Select the checkout's `.venv` Python in your
notebook interface. The Quarto CLI is a separate system installation; Python
dependencies do not install it or make historical CUDA training cells run on CPU.

## Develop and run tests

uv includes the development dependency group by default. Keep the same
all-extras environment for the optional pandas adapter and legacy tests:

```bash
uv sync --locked --all-extras
uv run --locked --all-extras pytest -v
uv run --locked --all-extras ty check src
uv run --locked --all-extras ruff check src tests
```

The automated numerical test suite runs on CPU. Passing those tests does not
establish GPU compatibility or scientific accuracy. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the build, installed-wheel checks and documentation workflow.
